assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a striking professional character concept sheet for ONE original playable fantasy species and ONE individual character for an adult multiplayer life-and-social RPG. Landscape 3:2 composition, with a dominant large full-body front three-quarter view occupying the left two thirds; on the right show a smaller consistent rear three-quarter view, and a large head study. Muted warm slate background with subtle ground shadows. No titles, labels, text, UI or logos. Fully show the main character's head, horns and feet. This is a bold game character design, not a cozy storybook illustration.

DESIGN: An adult bipedal highland RAM person, visibly animal-headed and anatomically nonhuman. Broad compact powerful torso, large heavy forearms and capable five-fingered hands, substantial bent hind limbs ending in broad cloven hooves. Around five-and-a-half heads tall. Coarse charcoal-blue fleece across the back of the neck and shoulders, pale ash-cream wool cheeks and chin, short dark sheep muzzle, wide bridge of nose, warm amber eyes with horizontal pupils, and broad side-pointing ears. TWO large weathered ram horns sweep outward then curl tightly BACK around the ears in a very readable circular ram-horn silhouette. Horns are ridged sandstone amber, the left horn has one weathered copper repair clasp. Absolutely not a bovine head, not a bull nose, not upright bull horns, not a human face with horns attached. Strong visible animal identity and calm adult intelligence. Expression is observant, gently amused and quietly capable, with restrained facial exaggeration. Powerful approachable presence. No plush-toy proportions or baby face.

CHARACTER IDENTITY: A highland lake fisher and pathfinder, someone the player would be curious to meet and happy to stand beside while fishing. Clothing must communicate his SPECIES and CULTURE, not a generic human costume. An asymmetrical short wrap mantle of dense storm-teal wool lies close against the torso, an exposed off-white woven underlayer and broad terracotta waist wrap. Low leather forearm wraps; fitted short divided lower garments end above the natural hooves, leaving the hooves visible. Clothing has broad planar material areas and just a few meaningful details. Woven storm-line patterns repeat a simple broken concentric curve motif that echoes the ram horns. No giant shoulder plates, no armor, no swords, no totem poles, no feathers or copied tribal insignia.
A worn bentwood fishing rod is carried casually in one hand, free of the body silhouette; beside the hip hangs a practical oval reed fish basket and a couple of dark river-stone net weights. One copper fishhook charm. All tools and garments are physically plausible and clearly separated. Do not overload the design with tiny belts, pouches and trinkets. Distinctive silhouette first, face second, material story third.

RENDERING: Sculptural stylized 3D game art, strong confident planes, broad hand-painted albedo color shapes, deliberate exaggerated anatomy and readable forms, like a production character art target that could be built as a real game model. Clearly defined fur clumps and horn rings with restrained detail. Strong soft directional light, charcoal-teal contrasted with ochre horn and a small terracotta accent. High craftsmanship and memorable species design. Avoid photoreal fur strands, cinematic live-action realism, generic medieval human villagers, Pixar/Disney facial design, anime, chibi, cute mascot, flat watercolor and children's-book painting. All three views must depict precisely the same individual, horn shapes, proportions, costume and color placement. Original species and individual, do not reproduce any existing game character or named fantasy race.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE original environment concept illustration for a third-person fantasy multiplayer life-and-social game. Wide landscape composition, 3:2 aspect ratio. A single coherent scene, no character sheet, no panels, no text or UI.

An extraordinary but inhabitable highland lakeside settlement built specifically by ram-headed humanoid people. It should feel elemental, rugged, welcoming and alive, with confident sculpted stylized 3D game forms, hand-painted color masses and readable real-time-game materials. Not a generic medieval human village.

CAMERA: third-person adventure gameplay perspective, a few meters behind one full-body ram fisherman in the lower-left foreground, environment dominates. The character has a compact powerful adult body, coarse charcoal-blue wool on neck and shoulders, cream wool cheeks, a dark SHORT SHEEP MUZZLE, amber eyes and TWO massive amber ridged RAM HORNS curling around the ears, broad five-fingered hands and CLOVEN HOOVES. His left horn has a small copper repair clasp. He wears a close-fitting teal wool wrap mantle with a simple cream broken-concentric-curve motif, a terracotta waist sash and brown short divided lower garments leaving the natural hooves exposed. Carries a simple bentwood fishing rod and an oval reed basket. No armor or weapons. He walks down a broad sloping stone path toward residents gathering at the lake.

The settlement occupies a grassy plateau above immense cliffs. Distant blue mountains and wind-carved mesas suggest a much larger world. A deep turquoise freshwater lake curves through the center-right. At the far shore is ONE unmistakable fantasy landmark: a great curved basalt arch, with a broken tip whose two small fragments levitate in the gap. Keep landmark in clear view.

Seven substantial low broad houses are nested into terraced rocky shelves around the lake. They have thick oval wind-carved sandstone foundations, broad rounded doors that accommodate ram horns, and CURVED WOODEN RIBS supporting wide low WOOL-FELT FAN-SHAPED ROOFS secured with copper joints and thick braided ropes. Some roofs have alpine turf. Curled beam ends and concentric carved lines echo ram horns. Restrained teal and rust cloth panels, warm wood, coarse woven fabrics and aged copper establish a coherent species culture. Windward stone walls shelter communal benches. Broad shallow stone steps and rough sloping paths fit cloven hooves. Include an open communal cookhouse with a hearth, a fish-net workshop and low shore landing terraces. Architecture must look like it was designed for this mountain species. No generic European cottages, no castles, no conical tents, no totem poles, no bull emblems or architecture copied from an existing game.

About twelve adult ram-folk residents with the same sheep muzzles, curly horns and cloven hooves, different coat colors and simple teal/rust everyday clothing. They gather naturally: three fish beside each other from a broad stone-and-timber lakeshore terrace; two mend a net; two sit talking near the fire; one waves a greeting to the foreground character. Readable gameplay-scale figures, not tiny dots and not a massive crowd. A place to stop and meet others.

Clear breezy late-morning directional sunlight, strong readable shadows, moving cloth pennants and wind-combed ochre-green grass. Cool slate and rich blue water balanced by warm stone and clay accents. Large deliberate shape design and believable human-scale spacing. Render as a polished sculptural stylized 3D game environment concept, not a soft children's-book painting, not photoreal live action, no sugary pastel prettiness, no toy village, no extreme bloom. Memorable original species, original architecture and original world.

CORE IDEA: This is the village built and lived in by the original ram-headed highland people in the reference. Every architectural and social choice should feel specific to their broad bodies, curling horns, cloven hooves and mountain-lake lives. CAMERA AND COMPOSITION: A grounded, slightly elevated third-person gameplay camera, close behind the referenced ram fisherman in the lower-left foreground. Show his full figure, from horns to hooves, occupying about one-fifth of the image height-to-width area rather than dominating the scene. WORLD AND ARCHITECTURE: Elevated plateau with immense cliffs and wide distant layered mountain horizons, wind-combed amber-green grass and a few hardy alpine trees. A deep blue freshwater lake fits naturally into the rocky plateau. A GREAT weather-worn curved basalt arch rises at the distant shore, its upper curve broken with two small stones gently suspended in the gap, providing one strong mysterious fantasy landmark. The village is near and tangible; the landmark is distant enough to invite future exploration.
About seven substantial, low, broad original buildings nested into terraced stone shelves, with circular-to-oval wind-carved gray sandstone bases and wide rounded doorways sized for curling horns. Curved laminated timber ribs support broad low wool-felt canopies shaped like layered fans, visibly tensioned with copper joints and heavy braided ropes; some roofs are partly covered with alpine turf. No conical tents. A few curled structural beam ends and broken concentric curve carvings echo the species' horns. Restrained teal and rust textile panels match the reference character. Broad shallow steps and rough ribbed stone paths suit cloven hooves. Windward stone walls shelter communal benches. A large cookhouse has an oval open hearth and vent, a fish-drying workshop faces a useful landing pier, homes look different in arrangement but share the same construction rules. Details show repaired, inhabited, interdependent lives. Not European chalet houses, castles, human tavern cliches, bull totems, giant tribal masks or any existing game's architecture.

COMMUNITY LIFE: About twelve adult ram-folk residents/players of the SAME species, with some coat-color, horn-age and clothing variations. Small natural clusters, not a staged lineup: three fishing side-by-side from a broad low stone-and-wood shore terrace; two repairing a net at the workshop; a broad older resident serving tea beside a sheltered communal fire; two seated talking near the path; a newcomer greeted by a resident. All have readable nonhuman ram heads, curling horns and cloven hooves. People are approximately normal gameplay distance, not tiny indistinct dots. No humans, no combat, no weapons, no merchant crowd of nameless stalls.

STYLE AND FEEL: Strong sculpted stylized real-time 3D game shapes and broad hand-painted material color zones, matching the reference's character rendering. Large readable masses, confident directional lighting, tactile stone, coarse woven wool, warm timber and aged copper. Clear breezy late-morning light with directional shadows, fresh highland air and some moving cloth. Natural ochre, slate gray, deep turquoise and rusty clay accents. The settlement should feel elemental, slightly strange, rugged and alive, with fantasy and welcoming community both visible. Avoid sugary pastoral picture-book prettiness, Disney/Pixar village aesthetics, photoreal cinematic realism, microscopic texture overload, exaggerated bloom, dreamy haze hiding shapes or luxury resort polish. Original strong environmental identity.
